paper_metadata.title: Variational quantum algorithm for unconstrained black box binary optimization: Application to feature selection

summary: The paper presents VarQFS, a variational gate-based quantum feature-selection method using a RealAmplitudes ansatz and QN-SPSA on the UCI German credit dataset. On the reduced 20-feature problem, the QPU run on ibmq montreal reached train/test log-loss 0.5351/0.5542, slightly better than RFE and RFECV; on the full 59-feature problem, the best MPS result at depth 2 achieved 0.4401 train and 0.4759 test, again outperforming the classical baselines reported in Table 4, but only in simulation and without a proven speedup.

experiments.description: Variational quantum feature selection (VarQFS) on a reduced 20-feature German credit-risk dataset, evaluated on both MPS simulation and IBM ibmq montreal hardware using a RealAmplitudes ansatz and QN-SPSA optimization.

algorithm.variant: Variational quantum feature selection (VarQFS) with QN-SPSA / quantum natural gradient approximation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: fixed 5,000 iterations for MPS; fixed 300 iterations for QPU
algorithm.parameter_initialization: initial state chosen to be uniform superposition over all basis states; parameters initialized to realize equal probability over all feature subsets

optimizer_settings.tolerance: discard updates that increase loss beyond twice the initial loss standard deviation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per feature; measured |1> includes the feature and |0> excludes it
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize empirical expected training loss over sampled feature subsets: L(θ)=Σ_m p_m(θ) S_train(x_m), where S_train is logistic-regression log-loss on the training set
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: implicitly defined diagonal Hamiltonian with diagonal entries f(x_j)=S_train(x_j)

problem_instance.description: Feature selection for German credit-risk classification on a reduced 20-feature subset chosen by RFECV(log-loss) from the full dataset

dataset_specification.description: 50% train / 50% test split; reduced 20-feature set selected as the 20 most important features by RFECV(log-loss) on the full training data

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: categorical attributes one-hot encoded in the full dataset; reduced set selected by RFECV(log-loss); train/test representativeness checked via Pearson correlation coefficients with at most ~10% variation between train and test
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 independent random seeds; 5,000 optimization iterations; 10,000 samples drawn after training to analyze sampling probabilities; statistical comparison on 1,000 data subsets with 70% of original train/test data; 95% confidence intervals via 50 bootstraps with 70% of train/test data

implementation_details.code_url: Qiskit public code referenced; exact repository URL not provided in paper
implementation_details.transpilation_target: ibmq_montreal coupling map / nearest-neighbor linear entanglement
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: one-hot encoding; RFECV used to select reduced 20-feature subset
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: best sampled feature subsets compared against RFE and RFECV baselines; confidence intervals computed by bootstrap

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: stochastic descent with outliers; generally decreasing

results.unit: seconds per gradient evaluation (without queueing, approximate)

speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports better feature-selection quality in some cases, but no computational speedup claim is demonstrated.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: not explicitly stated; variational optimization with polynomial-shot estimation and QN-SPSA approximate constant-cost gradient/QFI estimates
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: not explicitly stated; exhaustive search over 2^20 subsets feasible for reduced case, classical feature selection heuristics otherwise

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 20 logical qubits, depth-2 RealAmplitudes ansatz, 8,000 shots/iteration on ibmq montreal; 5,000 iterations in simulation and 300 on hardware
limiting_factors: Classical baselines are competitive and sometimes better on test metrics
Hardware run is small-scale and noisy
Objective evaluation requires repeated classical logistic-regression training

notes: Gate count total inferred as 60 single-qubit + 38 two-qubit gates = 98 for the depth-2 hardware experiment; paper explicitly states 60 one-qubit gates and 38 two-qubit gates.
The paper reports both MPS simulation and QPU results for the same experiment; hardware field records the QPU run, while the experiment description notes both backends.

Authors claim the method can outperform traditional feature selection in some examples, but the reported results are mixed: QPU achieves 0.5351 train / 0.5542 test versus RFECV(log) 0.5371 / 0.5562 and RFE 0.5371 / 0.5562 on the reduced set.
This is a small 20-feature benchmark, so it does not establish practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Variational quantum feature selection (VarQFS) on the full 59-feature one-hot-encoded German credit-risk dataset, evaluated with MPS simulation for ansatz depths 0, 1, and 2.

algorithm.variant: Variational quantum feature selection (VarQFS) with QN-SPSA / quantum natural gradient approximation
algorithm.parameter_initialization: initial state chosen to be uniform superposition over all basis states; parameters initialized to realize equal probability over all feature subsets

optimizer_settings.tolerance: discard updates that increase loss beyond twice the initial loss standard deviation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per feature; measured |1> includes the feature and |0> excludes it
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize empirical expected training loss over sampled feature subsets: L(θ)=Σ_m p_m(θ) S_train(x_m), where S_train is logistic-regression log-loss on the training set
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: implicitly defined diagonal Hamiltonian with diagonal entries f(x_j)=S_train(x_j)

problem_instance.description: Feature selection for German credit-risk classification on the full 59-feature one-hot-encoded dataset

dataset_specification.description: 50% train / 50% test split; full one-hot-encoded feature set of dimension 59

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: categorical attributes one-hot encoded; train/test representativeness checked via Pearson correlation coefficients with at most ~10% variation between train and test
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 independent random seeds for each depth; 5,000 optimization iterations; 10,000 samples drawn after training to analyze sampling probabilities; statistical comparison on 1,000 data subsets with 70% of original train/test data; 95% confidence intervals via 50 bootstraps with 70% of train/test data

implementation_details.code_url: Qiskit public code referenced; exact repository URL not provided in paper
implementation_details.transpilation_target: MPS simulator backend; exact transpilation settings not reported
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: best sampled feature subsets compared against RFE and RFECV baselines; confidence intervals computed by bootstrap

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: stochastic descent with outliers; generally decreasing

speedup_claims.caveats: No computational speedup is claimed; the paper reports improved feature-selection quality and scalability to 59 features via MPS simulation.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: not explicitly stated; variational optimization with polynomial-shot estimation and QN-SPSA approximate constant-cost gradient/QFI estimates
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: not explicitly stated; classical feature selection baselines RFE/RFECV used for comparison

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 59 logical qubits in MPS simulation, depth 0/1/2 RealAmplitudes, 10 seeds, 5,000 iterations, 10,000 shots/iteration
limiting_factors: No QPU result for the full 59-feature problem
Performance depends strongly on random seed

notes: The paper reports MPS simulation only for the full 59-feature case; no QPU run is described for this experiment.
Gate counts and transpiled depth are not reported for the full-data MPS runs.
The paper reports better sampled train/test scores than RFE/RFECV for some seeds, but this is only a simulation study and not a demonstrated practical advantage.
Reported best full-data MPS test score is 0.4759 at depth 2, compared with RFE 0.4848 and RFECV(acc) 0.4900.
